blockNote: Inventory management (Bank 03, 257943-258249): give an item or pickup (GiveItemToPlayer), remove an item by id (RemoveItemFromInventory) and test whether an item is held (CheckInventoryForItem).
=== CALLERS ===

GiveItemToPlayer has 10 JSL sites in 5 files: the COP GiveItem handler (cop_handlers_inventory), chests (warps_interaction), the NPC / pickup touch handler (combat_collision.InteractionDamage_NPCChat, which gives the gem and heal drops of DarkGemDropSystem), item_use_system and pyCD_puzzle (6). RemoveItemFromInventory and CheckInventoryForItem are reached only through their COP handlers.
=== ITEM ID ENCODING (A, low byte) ===

$00 to $7F: regular items, stored in the first free slot of the 16-byte inventorySlots ($0AB4). $80 = HP Max Up, $81 = STR Up, $82 = DEF Up (each +1). $83 / $84 / $85 = 1 / 2 / 5 gems (gemCount capped at 999). $86 and above = heal: hpToHeal += 5 plus the SpawnHitSparkSprites effect. After the PHP / SEP #$20 prologue the code tests bit 7 of the id and, for specials, subtracts $80 and walks a DEC chain.
=== STAT-UP ITEMS ===

Each one clears displayModeFlags bit $0080 (leave the display-filter actor mode, in which RunActors_Normal runs only actors flagged $1000; the chest code in warps_interaction sets it around the call), plays SFX $25, adds 1 to the 8-bit stat and returns with Y = 0. The add is 8-bit signed: only when the old value is $7F does the overflow flag trigger and the stat is set to $55 (85) instead. That is a reset, not a cap: below $7F and above it (wrapping at $FF to 0) the stat is unbounded. The old note called it a cap at $55.
HP Max Up also sets hpToHeal := new max HP - HP (an 8-bit difference), so UpdateHUD refills the bar to the new maximum at 1 HP every 8 frames. STR Up and DEF Up do not touch hpToHeal.
=== OTHER SPECIAL ITEMS ===

Gems add 1, 2 or 5 to gemCount, clamp at $03E7 and play SFX $22. The heal ($86 and above) adds 5 to hpToHeal, switches D to the calling actor (D := X) so that COP SpawnListAppend( SpawnHitSparkSprites, #00, #00, flags $2F00 ) creates the sparkle at that actor, and plays SFX $22. X must therefore be the calling actor's slot on this path. Neither the gems nor the heal change Y or $0DB8.
=== RETURN CONVENTION ===

Carry clear = given, carry set = inventory full. Regular items: Y = dialogstring_01FF1F (success), $0DB8 = item id ($0DB9 = 0) for the dialogue text; full inventory: Y = dialogstring_01FF02, $0DB8 = item id. Stat-ups return Y = 0; gems and the heal leave Y as the caller had it, so a caller must not show Y for ids of $80 and above. P is restored (PLP).

RemoveItemFromInventory: first slot equal to A is zeroed and, only then, inventoryEquippedType := 0 and inventoryEquippedIndex := $FFFF (nothing equipped); a missing id changes nothing, and in both cases carry is restored by the PLP (the routine reports nothing). CheckInventoryForItem: carry clear = found, carry set = not found.

GiveItemToPlayer: Give the item whose id is in A (low byte). Regular ids $00 to $7F go into the first empty slot of inventorySlots; ids from $80 are specials, decoded as id - $80: 0 HP Max Up, 1 STR Up, 2 DEF Up (GiveItem_DefUp), 3 / 4 / 5 = 1 / 2 / 5 gems, 6 and up = heal 5 HP with the spark effect.
Returns carry clear = given, carry set = inventory full; Y = dialogue string for regular items and for the full case. Details in the block note.

blockNote: Reusable town-NPC wander behaviour (Bank 00, 50968-51193) used by 13 ambient NPC actors in Dao (daC9_businessman, daC3_man1), Watermia (wa78 water_kid, moving_woman, glass_game, centipede_man), Angel Village (av6B villagers2, ocean_ache), Euro (eu91 women2, men2), Seaside Palace (sp5A_villagers) and South Cape (sc01_roof_man, sc04_poverty).
=== CALLING PATTERN ===

The NPC's init stores its base animation index in currentHp,X ($7F0026) and calls SyncActorPosFromDP once. Its loop is: JSL NpcRandomWanderAI, SetEntryHereAndYield, SetEntryHere, AnimOnce, BRA loop. The routines here only choose and stage; the caller's AnimOnce plays the staged animation.
=== DATA ===

$7F0010 / $7F0012 (mnemonics orbitAngle / orbitDiameter, there is no orbit here) hold the home X / Y that SyncActorPosFromDP copies from DP $14 / $16. $7F0026 (mnemonic currentHp) is the NPC's base animation index. The sprite sheet is laid out as base + 0 to 3 = stand south / north / west / east and base + 4 to 7 = walk south / north / west / east.
=== DECISION ===

NpcRandomWanderAI rolls RngByte and 7 (each case has probability 1/8) and runs COP SwitchCase on the byte at $0000. The table is: 0 = stand north, 1 = stand south, 2 = stand west, 3 = stand east, 4 = step north, 5 = step south, 6 = step west, 7 = step east (the old note listed cases 4 to 7 as south / north / west / east; cases 4 and 5 are north and south, and cases 0 and 1 are the stand pair north and south).

Standing: $28 := base + direction, $2A := 0, UpdateActorAnimation, $08 := $78 (the script sleeps 120 frames after the caller's SetEntryHereAndYield) and MarkSolidHere (a standing NPC blocks the player).

Stepping: if the NPC is already more than $30 pixels (3 tiles) from its home in that direction, or the BranchIfSolid test for that side finds a solid tile, it stands facing that direction instead. Otherwise it stages a movement delta chain (StageMoveX / StageMoveY #$11 = +1 pixel every second frame, east or south; #$12 = -1 every second frame, west or north), sets the walk animation (base + 4 to 7), and does ClearSolidHere (a walking NPC is not solid).

The step lasts for one pass of the walk animation: the caller's AnimOnce moves the NPC at half a pixel per frame until the animation list ends, then clears the chain ($2C / $2E) and the loop rolls again. The step length is therefore half the number of frames of the walk animation, in pixels, and there is no re-roll in the middle of a step (the old note said 'one-tile forced move').

blockNote: Camera drift library (Bank 00, 53134-53350): three short-lived actor scripts that nudge the camera during set pieces. Scene scripts spawn them with SpawnAfterFlags / SpawnListAppend; each dies when finished.
=== CALLERS ===

CameraDriftLoopSimple: pyCD_flame_statue, ir25_ceiling_tile, ir29_castoth. CameraDriftLoopShip: st68_kara (Angel Village undersea tunnel), gs2D_lily, gs2D_lance, gs2B_erik (Gold Ship). CameraDriftPatterned: awB1_gorgon, pyD9_dangerslide_controller, ir29_castoth (3 sites).
=== VARIABLES ===

cameraTargetX / Y ($06BE / $06C2) are the scroll targets (camera_scroll_controller recomputes them each frame) and cameraDeltaX / Y ($06C0 / $06C4) the per-frame scroll deltas that the visual_effect_pipeline actors integrate. These are not the effectDeltaX / Y ($06E4 / $06E6) that camera_scroll_controller writes. Whether the offsets added here survive that recompute is not established statically (OQ-I050-2).
=== CameraDriftLoopSimple ===

LoopStart #$78 runs 120 passes, one frame each (every LoopEnd pass yields). Each pass adds r = (RngByte and 3) - 1, that is -1, 0, +1 or +2 (bias +0.5), to cameraTargetY and to cameraDeltaY. Nothing is undone at the end. The same formula is the Y shake in player_character. Then Die. The old note said 'random +-1'.
=== CameraDriftLoopShip ===

Sets $12 bit $1000 (the display / overlay-active qualifier, so the drift also runs in the display-filtered modes) and $26 := 0 ($26 = the offset applied last frame). 120 passes: while playerFlags bit $0100 (forced walk) is set a pass does nothing; otherwise cameraDeltaY -= $26 (undo last frame), $26 := RngByte and 3 (0 to 3), then cameraTargetY += $26 and cameraDeltaY += $26. After the loop it yields once (SetEntryHereAndYield), subtracts the last $26 from cameraDeltaY and dies. So the delta offset is temporary (each frame replaces the previous one) while the target offset is not undone here.
=== CameraDriftPatterned ===

$28 := RngByte (random starting phase), $2A := 2, SetEntryHere. Each run: DBR := program bank (to read binary_00D068), Y offset := table[$28 and 7] then $28++, added to cameraTargetY (a negative result is clamped to 0) and, unless $24 = $FFFF, to cameraDeltaY (clamped to 0); then the X offset := table[$28 and 7], i.e. the next entry, with the same rules. A run is followed by $08 := 3 (3 frames) and DEC $2A; the third run ends in Die, so the actor lives about 9 frames and applies 3 Y and 3 X offsets. The next run's Y entry is the previous run's X entry.

binary_00D068 holds 16 words but the index is masked to 3 bits, so only the first 8 are used: +1, -1, -2, +1, +2, 0, -2, +1 (sum 0). The last 8 words (+5, -4, -2, +4, +1, -5, +4, -3, also summing to 0) are never read.
